newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears aid to Alitalia, imposes conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU clears aid to Alitalia, imposes conditions.

text.p: The European Commission cleared the payment of 2.75 trillion lire of state to Italian flag carrier Alitalia on Tuesday, imposing various conditions in return for approval of the state-funded injection.

Aid clearance, widely signalled in advance after the successful conclusion of negotiations between the Commission and the Rome government, included a requirement that the airline sell its holding in the Hungarian carrier MALEV, a statement said.

Payment of the aid will come in three tranches of two trillion, 500 billion and 250 billion lire respectively, the first due immediately and including one trillion already paid in June 1996, the statement added.
"The remainder will be conditional on the satisfactory progress of the company's restructuring plan and on the respect of a series of conditions," the statement added.

"This decision should close the cycle of state aid applications that has characterised the efforts by European airlines to restructure and meet the challenges of global competition," European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said in the statement.

"Practically all European carriers have made radical internal changes in recent years," Kinnock said, a reference to a series of aid clearances in which has seen cash injections to Spain's Iberia, Air Franc, TAP Air Portugal, Greece's Olympic Airways and Ireland's Aer Lingus.
